types.embedding_query_text: Award Ceremony: A formal event where awards are presented to recognize achievements in a particular field. Also called Awards Show, Gala, Prize Giving, Ceremony. Examples: Primetime Emmy Awards, 78th Annual Primetime Emmy Awards, Emmy Awards, Emmys.

chosen_type.label: AwardCeremony
chosen_type.definition: A formal event where awards are presented to recognize achievements.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class specifically represents an award ceremony; 'Event' is too broad, and other event types are too specific. Minting a new type with 'Event' as parent.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ExhibitionEvent
candidates.comment: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

types.embedding_query_text: Group of Individuals/Works: A collection of people or creative works that are considered together, often for a specific purpose like nominations. Also called Collection, Set, Selection, List. Examples: nominees.

chosen_type.label: Collection
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Collection' class accurately describes a grouping of individuals or works, fitting 'nominees'.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: MusicPlaylist
candidates.comment: A MusicPlaylist, as a CreativeWork, is an ordered collection of music tracks. Also called playlist, music compilation, track list. Examples: a Spotify playlist, a radio station's daily playlist, a custom mix CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is a formally released collection of tracks.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: CreativeWork
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual or artistic creation, encompassing a wide range of media and forms. Also called artistic work, intellectual property, creation, content. Examples: A novel, a film, a photograph, a piece of software, a song, a painting.

types.embedding_query_text: News Organization: An entity responsible for gathering, reporting, and disseminating news and information. Also called Media Company, News Agency, Broadcaster, Publisher. Examples: CNN.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'NewsMediaOrganization' class is a direct and precise match for the definition and example 'CNN'.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day, month, and year. Also called Calendar Day, Day, Specific Day. Examples: Wednesday, 2026-07-11, 11/07/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Date' datatype directly matches the definition 'A specific day, month, and year', and fits the example '2026-07-11'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Industry: A sector of the economy that produces goods or services. Also called Sector, Business, Trade, Field. Examples: Hollywood.

chosen_type.definition: A broad classification of businesses based on the primary economic activity they engage in.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents an 'Industry' as a sector of the economy; existing business types are too specific. Minting a new type with 'Thing' as parent.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: Casino
candidates.comment: A local business primarily offering gambling activities and often entertainment. Also called gambling house, gaming establishment, resort casino. Examples: Bellagio, Caesars Palace, Monte Carlo Casino.

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet

candidates.comment: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.

candidates.label: BroadcastChannel
candidates.comment: A BroadcastChannel is an Intangible entity representing a specific instance of a BroadcastService within a cable or satellite lineup. Also called TV channel, radio station frequency, media channel. Examples: BBC One, CNN, ESPN, local public radio station.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: TVSeries
candidates.comment: A creative work series dedicated to television broadcast and associated online delivery, comprising multiple seasons and episodes. Also called television show, TV program, broadcast series. Examples: 'Game of Thrones', 'The Office', 'Stranger Things'.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity of Awards: A numerical count of the awards received by an individual or entity. Also called Award Count, Number of Prizes, Trophy Tally. Examples: four Emmys.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Quantity' datatype represents measurable amounts, which aligns with 'A numerical count of the awards received'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: AggregateRating
candidates.comment: An AggregateRating is a Rating that represents the average or summary of multiple individual ratings or reviews. Also called average rating, collective rating, summary score, overall rating. Examples: A product's 4.5-star rating based on 100 reviews, a movie's Rotten Tomatoes score, a restaurant's Yelp rating. Distinct from Rating, which is a single individual rating.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A specific calendar year. Also called Annual Period, Yearly Date. Examples: 1998, 2026.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class specifically represents a 'Year' as a standalone concept; 'Date' is too specific. 'Date' is the closest parent for a time-related datatype.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity of Nominations: A numerical count of the nominations received by an individual or entity. Also called Nomination Count, Number of Nods, Nomination Tally. Examples: 19 nominations.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Quantity' datatype represents measurable amounts, which aligns with 'A numerical count of the nominations received'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: ReservationStatusType
candidates.comment: ReservationStatusType is a StatusEnumeration listing enumerated status values for a Reservation. Also called booking status, reservation state. Examples: ReservationConfirmed, ReservationPending, ReservationCancelled, ReservationHold.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: CertificationStatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration defining the possible statuses of a certification. Also called certification state, approval status, credential status. Examples: Active, Inactive, Expired, Pending.

types.embedding_query_text: Fictional Character Role: The specific part or persona portrayed by an actor within a fictional work. Also called Character Part, Role Played, Fictional Persona. Examples: mayor of an island, menacing billionaire, steely US ambassador.

chosen_type.label: PerformanceRole
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'PerformanceRole' class is a perfect match for the definition and examples of a 'Fictional Character Role'.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Abstract, Theme. Examples: supernatural phenomena, nominations.

chosen_type.label: Concept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or general notion.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an abstract 'Concept'. 'Thing' is the most general parent for abstract entities.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: Episode
candidates.comment: An Episode is a CreativeWork representing a single installment of a media series, such as a TV show, radio program, or video game. Also called installment, segment, part. Examples: A single episode of a TV series, a chapter in a podcast, a level in a video game series.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

types.embedding_query_text: DateTime: A specific point in time, including both date and time components. Also called Timestamp, Moment, Point in Time. Examples: Monday, September 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT.

chosen_type.label: DateTime
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'DateTime' datatype is a perfect match for the definition and example of a specific point in time including date and time.

mentions: Monday, September 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Association, Institution, Company, Body. Examples: Television Academy.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Organization' class is a perfect match for the definition and example 'Television Academy'.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

types.embedding_query_text: Website: A set of related web pages served from a single web domain. Also called Web Portal, Online Site, Internet Site. Examples: Television Academy website.

chosen_type.label: WebSite
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'WebSite' class is a perfect match for the definition and example of a website.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: ItemPage
candidates.comment: An ItemPage is a web page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel. Also called product page, detail page, single item view. Examples: an Amazon product page, a hotel booking page for a specific hotel, a blog post about one topic. Distinct from CollectionPage, which displays multiple items.

candidates.label: AboutPage
candidates.comment: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. Examples: The "About Us" section of a company website, a personal biography page, a project overview page.

candidates.label: ContactPage
candidates.comment: A web page specifically designed to provide contact information for an entity. Also called contact us page, inquiry page, reach us page. Examples: A website's "Contact Us" page, a business's support page, a personal portfolio's contact section. Distinct from WebPage, which is a general web document.
